_meta.companion: data/telescopes/oschin.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows vista.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; oschin: title, telescope (machine-readable stop, mirror, correctors, pupil, foci; refs point to sourced params as 'oschin.<param>'), explorer_preset (the proposed web/tpresets.js entry, evaluated from the js block in the .md), drawing, params, not_found, conflicts, notes.
_meta.rule: Each value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/telescopes/oschin/ (six byte-identical copies from rawdata/imaging/poss/ and rawdata/imaging/ztf/, marked in the cite). derived = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). figure_readoff = a value read off a saved figure, photograph or image (its caption or header is checked). INFERRED = a choice no source states. NOT FOUND marks a gap. Nothing is filled from memory.
_meta.quote_normalization: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, primes, dashes, minus, multiplication sign (to x), approximately-equal and tilde operators, micro and mu (to u), the degree sign and ring operator, middle dot and plus-minus normalized; soft hyphens removed; whitespace collapsed; a quote also passes against the text with line-end hyphenation closed up or kept, or with all whitespace removed; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces. OCR quotes keep the OCR's errors, flagged in notes

explorer_preset.name: Oschin 48-inch Schmidt
explorer_preset.primaryNote: A spherical Pyrex mirror, aluminized, 72 inches (1.83 m) across with a 6.12 m radius of curvature (f = 3.06 m). The stop is the corrector plate 6.12 m in front, at the mirror's center of curvature; the mirror is larger than the stop so that the beams of stars up to 2.7° off the axis fall wholly on the mirror. Completed in 1948.
explorer_preset.pupilNote: The ZTF era, seen from the mirror with the CCD rows horizontal (east–west): the 1.245 m stop less the camera's shadow and three 27 mm spider vanes. The camera is drawn as the octagonal cryostat window (483 × 442 mm) with a 20 mm border, the size that blocks the published 20.2% of the pupil; the vane width blocks the published 2.3%. One vane runs north–south; whether toward north or south is not published.

Neither the holder's size nor the vanes' width is published: the holder is drawn as the 14-inch plate (a lower bound) and the vanes 20 mm wide (a rough reading of a photograph).

foci.secondary: none (one mirror): at the stop, the original singlet plate of 3/8-inch plate glass, figured on both sides
foci.where: inside the tube, halfway between the corrector and the mirror, facing the mirror: the plateholder on a four-vane focus hub
foci.fieldNote: The 14-inch plates cover 6.6° × 6.6°; drawn is the 5.4° unvignetted field, and the plate corners lose 0.1–0.2 mag. The singlet corrector was figured for blue light (4358 Å in Harrington 1952; 4861 Å in the 1954 Atlas), so the image quality degrades in the red and near-infrared. The 1 mm glass plates were bent in the plateholder to the spherical focal surface (radius 3.07 m), drawn flat.

drawing: imager.js design "schmidt" places the stop (an ideal corrector of no power) at z = -2f, the spherical mirror at 0 and the focus at f, all from F and D: node runs of `IM.design` with the proposed entries give f = 3061.7 mm (ZTF) and 3069.9 mm (plates), the stop 6123.4 and 6139.9 mm in front of the mirror (6124 mm in D20, 6125.5 mm in H52) and the focus 3061.7 and 3069.9 mm from the mirror; one star, one point (spread 0). imgapp.js draws the mirror as large as the field's bundles at the mirror (x 1.02): 1864 mm (ZTF, field 327') and 1873 mm (plates, 324'), compared with the real 1828.8 mm, so the drawing shows the mirror larger than the stop for the reason the real one is. The prime-focus box (pfu) at the focus is max(drawEps D/2, 1.2 x the field's half-width) tall: 559 mm for ZTF (the real cryostat window is 483 x 442 mm), 401 mm for the plateholder.

What the drawing shows faithfully: the stop at the corrector, the oversized spherical mirror 2f behind the stop, the focus halfway and facing the mirror, the plateholder or camera in the incoming beam (the obstruction), the beams of the field's center and edge walking across the mirror, and the pupil with the block and vanes (2D panel and 3D view).

Schematic in the drawing, per focus. ZTF: the corrector is drawn as one thin plate of no power (really the cemented doublet plus the air-spaced trim plate, an aspheric triplet); the focal surface is drawn flat (really a sphere of radius 3062 mm, flattened to 7000 mm by the 32 mm meniscus window, then by a plano-convex field flattener over each CCD on a faceted cold plate: none drawn); the filter, the window and the hexapod are not drawn; the camera box is as tall as the area-equivalent circle of the published 20.2% (559 mm), and the pupil block is the window octagon with an INFERRED border; the three vanes are raked in the telescope and drawn in one plane at the camera (3D) or in the pupil; the field drawn is the 5.45 deg unvignetted circle (the mosaic is 7.32 x 7.50 deg). POSS-II: the corrector drawn as one plate (really the cemented achromatic doublet); the plates' spherical surface (R = 120.9 in) drawn flat; the filter in the plateholder not drawn; the plateholder box and the pupil block are the 14-in plate (INFERRED lower bound); vanes 20 mm (INFERRED). POSS-I: as POSS-II with the singlet plate (whose chromatic error the ideal drawing does not show); the two plate foci draw identically. The clam-shell (plates) and bi-parting (ZTF) shutters at the corrector are not drawn; the tube (6.65 m long, 2.1 m across) is not drawn.

No new drawing code is needed: the Schmidt branch exists in imager.js, imgapp.js and tel3d.js, and the blocks and per-focus pupils exist in tpupil.js and telapp.js. A curved focal surface (with the ZTF window and flatteners) would need a curved focus element in the Schmidt branch of imgapp.js and tel3d.js.

notes: A Schmidt's stop is the corrector at the mirror's center of curvature (6.12 m in front of the mirror); the focus lies halfway, inside the tube, facing the mirror. The mirror (1.83 m) is larger than the stop (1.24-1.26 m) because each field angle uses a different part of the mirror: a beam at 2.7 deg walks 6.124 m x tan 2.7 deg = 0.29 m across the mirror (DERIVED), which sets the unvignetted field (5.34-5.45 deg, DERIVED; 5.4 deg published).

The obstruction is the plateholder or camera in the incoming beam, between the corrector and the mirror; the returning beam converges onto the same object from the other side. The obstruction therefore shadows the pupil's center at each field angle, and the shadow grows off the axis (ZTF: 22.4% on axis, ~46% at the field's edge).
The four plate-era vanes give four diffraction spikes along north-south and east-west (DSS1V, DSS2V); the three ZTF vanes give six (ZTFV; D20 Sec. 4.1). The ZTF spikes include an east-west pair.

POSS-I and POSS-II used the same stop, mirror, focal length, plates and four-vane hub; the corrector (singlet vs achromatic doublet), the mandrels (reground for POSS-II) and the filter's place (in the POSS-II plateholder) changed. In the explorer the two foci differ only in their text.

The CCD eras between the plates and ZTF are not proposed as foci: NEAT (from 2000-2001), QUEST (two years later) and the PTF camera (2008 until ZTF; the CFH12K mosaic behind a powered dewar window on the four-vane hub, B19 and D20; 19% obstruction, S14) (PAL).
